claim_being_audited: The model can be certified for launch without resolving or disclosing the HR benefits enrollment weakness because aggregate readiness passed, rehearsal had no severity-one incidents, and public AI governance guidance supports certify-with-monitoring.
decision_criteria: A material weakness affecting a named launch use case requires either resolution, disclosure, or approved risk acceptance before launch.
General readiness evidence may support launch preparedness, but it cannot cure a missing policy-required disclosure decision.
Open legal review and named customer commitments weigh against treating the weakness as immaterial on the current record.
evidence_requests: Provide the actual pre-launch model card or disclosure showing the HR benefits enrollment weakness was disclosed.
Provide approved risk acceptance documentation covering this named launch use case before launch.
Provide the final legal determination closing review on whether disclosure was required.
Provide the exact certification artifact showing how the materiality predicate was evaluated against policy.
specific_concerns: The admissible summary shows the affected HR benefits enrollment segment misses target by 1.5 percentage points.
The affected segment is described as a named launch use case in two employer rollout commitments, which meets the policy's materiality trigger.
Legal review is still open, and the policy text says non-core or low-volume labels do not resolve materiality when legal review is pending.
No admissible evidence is provided that the weakness was disclosed before launch or that an approved risk acceptance covered the gap.
Aggregate readiness and absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents support general launch readiness, but they do not satisfy the specific policy predicate for a material weakness disclosure.
unsupported_claims: That certification is policy-compliant on the present record.
That public model-card or NIST-style monitoring guidance can substitute for the required disclosure or approved risk acceptance.
Any implied conclusion that Product's non-core characterization defeats materiality for this named launch use case.
